correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives exact cofactor and unit Floquet multiplier. Taylor expansion of polar scalar ODE and variation of constants prove K(t). The exact trigonometric moment gives K(t) ~ -pi*t^2/2; a unique nondegenerate maximizer of H and a quadratic zero of its amplitude yield positive Gaussian-Laplace asymptotics. Independently deriving an attracting origin via cubic radius return and using two disjoint open basins plus Poincare-Bendixson forces an interior periodic orbit. Verified standalone symbolic identities; numerical quadrature is illustrative, not used as proof.

value.rationale: The neutral unit-circle Floquet multiplier cannot detect one-sided attraction. Its rigorous reversal as coupling grows produces competing attractors and forces a previously undetected interior periodic orbit, a structurally motivated counterpoint to a published uniqueness conclusion based on perturbative Melnikov data. This is not a routine perturbative sign check: the decisive sign comes from an exponentially large strong-parameter Laplace integral.
